audit_notes: Model: through-thickness shear of the topcoat under a sliding contact with traction mu*p: u'' = 0, u(0) = 0 at the primer, G u'(1)/t = mu*p at the surface. The shear stress transmitted into the coating (and to the primer interface) equals mu*p: design 0.02*0.2 MPa = 4 kPa, baseline 0.4*0.2 MPa = 80 kPa, gain 95 % by construction, entirely set by the ratio of friction coefficients. This is the honest limit of a 1D model: the benefit is a tribological input, not a simulated result. Checks: shear strain in the baseline, 80 kPa/0.33 MPa = 0.24, elastic but a large cyclic strain for a soft silicone under brushes; with hydration lubrication 0.012. Tearing of soft silicones under sliding contact starts where traction exceeds a few tens of kPa near asperity edges, so the reduction is meaningful for durability if the lubricating layer survives. Caveats: (1) mu = 0.02 is from clean lab tribometry with smooth counterfaces; sand, debris and biofilm in the contact raise it; (2) the PC layer is itself abraded by the contacts; (3) contact pressure under fenders can exceed 1 MPa, where hydration layers of polymer brushes (not liposomes) may be squeezed out. Dimensionless: friction ratio 20; shear strain 0.012 (design) vs 0.24 (baseline). Simulation coefficient: design traction 4000 Pa (informational).
